answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it may submit bids, vote, or claim rewards. If an identity is caught double-signing or violating a task’s rules, its deposit is forfeited; creating more identities therefore multiplies the capital at risk rather than multiplying influence for free. Honest agents can keep deposits locked while serving a lotus garden project or competing at a summit, but a sybil attacker must tie up real funds in each identity and may lose them when misconduct is proven.
